title: With no IOMMU unit in service, standard and server images let a claimed PCI device DMA to all RAM
preconditions: Machine with no DMAR/IVRS unit in service or firmware-owned unit
Standard or server image (carries nonos-dma-unconfined-posture), boot profile Standard
A compromised driver capsule holding Dma and a claimed bus-master device
description: When no unit enforces, verdict() returns Unconfined for a PCI claim and MkDmaMap returns the physical address. There is no software fallback. Hardened and airgapped profiles drop the posture; external-port devices are refused even under it (unconfined.rs:16-21).
impact: Compromise of one DMA-capable driver capsule on such a machine gives read and write of all physical memory, including kernel text, and is now shown to crash the kernel (a device write into the kernel's own executable code led to a fatal page fault and a power-off). Documented design limit (release notes 0.9.3-security-limits.md:11-21; the boot serial prints the posture). On VT-d/AMD-Vi machines with remapping on, the same write is blocked and recorded as a fault, and the kernel keeps running.
scenario: Boot on hardware without a usable remapping unit.
A driver capsule is compromised, sets bus master and programs DMA with a physical address from MkDmaMap.

steps: Code and docs read and confirmed by an independent reading.
Dev-build boots printed 'no DMAR: posture=dma-unconfined' without a remapping unit, and enforcing=1 with the VT-d/AMD-Vi lanes.

Reproduced on a booted kernel: a claimed device under the no-IOMMU posture was granted a raw physical address and used to overwrite a kernel page (first shown on a kernel clock-info page: the page's contents were replaced; under the VT-d lane the same write was blocked and the original contents were intact).

Taken further on a booted kernel: the same device was pointed at the physical address of the kernel's own executable code. Under the no-IOMMU posture, the device's write landed, the kernel then executed the overwritten bytes, hit a fatal page fault, and powered off. Under the VT-d lane, the identical write attempt was blocked and logged as an IOMMU fault, and the kernel kept running.

Not shown: a device that lets the capsule choose the written bytes (this test's device supplies pseudo-random data), so controlled-content code execution remains a traced path, not a demonstrated one.

remediation: Make the posture an explicit build choice with a boot refusal on Standard profile, or add a software bounce-buffer path.
